legal_basis: Karnataka Rent Act, 1999 and Bengaluru residential rental market norms, read with Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (reasonable compensation for breach). The Act does not cap security deposits, notice symmetry, or exit painting charges, so those rules are labelled `above_local_norm` — a market-norm deviation, not a statutory conflict.

rules.title: Deposit far exceeds local norm
rules.detection_hint: If the refundable security deposit is more than three months' rent, flag the excess. The Bengaluru and Karnataka market norm is two to three months; a ten-month deposit is a local-norm deviation even though the Act itself sets no cap.

negotiation_ask.short_title: Cap the deposit at three months
negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could we set the deposit to three months' rent instead of ten? That matches the usual Bengaluru practice and is easier for both of us.
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: A ten-month deposit is far above the local norm of two to three months. Please revise Clause {clause_ref} to a maximum of three months' rent.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: The Tenant shall pay an interest-free security deposit equal to three (3) months' rent, refundable under the terms of this Agreement.

rules.title: Eleven-month lock-in with four-month penalty
rules.detection_hint: Flag any lock-in that forfeits more than one month's rent on early exit, and any lock-in that binds only the tenant while the owner may exit freely. Section 74 limits a penalty to a reasonable estimate of the loss actually caused by the breach.

negotiation_ask.short_title: Replace lock-in with an exit notice
negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could we replace the four-month lock-in penalty with a two-month notice period, so either side can exit fairly?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: A four-month forfeiture is disproportionate to actual loss under Section 74. Please replace Clause {clause_ref}'s lock-in penalty with a one-month notice-based exit.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving one (1) month's written notice. No separate lock-in penalty shall apply.

rules.title: Notice period applies only to the Tenant

benchmark.typical_label: Same notice period for both parties

statutory_citation.section: No statutory notice-symmetry mandate — Bengaluru market norm

rules.detection_hint: Flag agreements where a notice period binds only the tenant, or where the owner may terminate on materially shorter notice than the tenant. A one-sided notice obligation leaves the tenant without matching protection; the Act itself does not mandate symmetry.

negotiation_ask.short_title: Make notice the same for both sides
negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could the three-month notice apply to both of us, so it is fair on both sides?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: Clause {clause_ref} imposes three months' notice only on the Tenant. Please make the notice period symmetric for both parties.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: Either party shall provide three (3) months' written notice before terminating this Agreement.

rules.title: No deadline for returning the deposit

statutory_citation.act: Indian Contract Act, 1872; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
statutory_citation.section: Unfair trade practice — open-ended deposit retention

rules.detection_hint: Flag agreements that do not state a fixed number of days for returning the deposit after handover, or that allow deductions without an itemised written statement. Open-ended refund language is the most common cause of post-handover deposit disputes.

negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could we add that the deposit will be returned within 15 days of handover, with any deductions listed in writing?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: Clause {clause_ref} leaves the deposit refund open-ended. Please add a 15-day deadline after handover with an itemised deduction statement.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: Any refundable deposit shall be returned, after lawful and itemised deductions (if any), within fifteen (15) days of handover.

rules.title: Fixed painting charge at exit

benchmark.typical_label: Actual cost with receipts, normal wear excluded

statutory_citation.section: No fixed painting-charge mandate — local norm is actual cost with receipts

rules.detection_hint: Flag fixed painting, cleaning or repainting charges payable at exit, especially where the amount is pre-set regardless of the flat's actual condition. The fair benchmark is receipt-backed actual cost with normal wear and tear excluded.

negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could the painting charge be based on actual cost with receipts, excluding normal wear and tear?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: A fixed ₹40,000 painting charge is above the local norm. Please revise Clause {clause_ref} to actual, receipt-backed cost excluding normal wear.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: The Tenant shall bear only the actual, receipt-supported cost of repainting required beyond normal wear and tear.

expected_clauses.label: Specific deposit refund timeline
expected_clauses.why_it_matters: Open-ended refund language delays refunds after handover.

expected_clauses.label: Symmetric notice period
expected_clauses.why_it_matters: One-sided notice lets the stronger party exit without giving the weaker party time to plan.

expected_clauses.label: Dispute resolution and jurisdiction
expected_clauses.why_it_matters: Without a specified forum, disputes default to the drafting party's home court, which may be far away.
